overnightPermit.what: Olympic National Park wilderness camping permit, reserved in advance with a nightly per-person fee
overnightPermit.where: Reserve on Recreation.gov or by phone with the Wilderness Information Center, and print it from your account; no same-day walk-up sites are held, and Sol Duc/Seven Lakes Basin and the East Fork Quinault are quota areas.

add.notes: Established camp on the West Fork Dosewallips trail about 8 miles past the old ranger station, below Anderson Pass. The usual base for the Anderson Glacier side of the massif.

add.permit: Olympic National Park wilderness permit required
add.notes: Meadow basin with tarns below Mount Ferry on the Bailey Range traverse. The usual camp for Pulitzer and Ferry, reached by off-trail travel from High Divide.

routes.note: Every listed camp is on the Elwha or Quinault side; Pulitzer is climbed from Ferry Basin, added without an elevation because the existing records disagree (5,400 vs 5,700 ft).

add.name: Seattle Meadows
add.capacity: A few tent sites in meadow
add.permit: Olympic National Park wilderness permit required
add.notes: High camp in Upper Seattle Basin above Seattle Creek, below the summit's west side. The closest camp to the peak.

routes.note: Seattle Creek is a Quinault tributary reached from the North Fork Quinault trail, so Elwha camps drop; Seattle Meadows added as the high camp in this basin, listed after Low Divide which is more used.
